notes: Self-test prompt set for the eval harness. 2 positive / 2 negative, 3 trials each. The transcripts under ../cases/ are SYNTHETIC (hand-authored by generate.py, no model produced them) and are marked as such in every meta sidecar, so the runner refuses them unless --allow-synthetic-fixtures is passed. They exercise the harness's grading path — trigger detection, outcome checks, the positive-rate gate, the artifact binding — and say NOTHING about any real skill's trigger behaviour.

cases.prompt: here is the artifact I mentioned, https://example.invalid/paper.pdf — see what you make of it
cases.rationale: Fires on turn 1 and produces artifact-touching tool inputs (WebFetch of the URL, Write to a .md), so the input-inspecting outcome checks have something real to grade.

cases.prompt: dropping the spec at docs/inbox/example-spec.md, thoughts on how it lands for us
cases.rationale: Fires on turn 5, not turn 1 — locks 'outcomes, not paths' into the committed set, so a future change that starts grading the route breaks CI.

cases.prompt: fix the null dereference in parser.py, it throws on an empty buffer
cases.rationale: A fully-specified engineering task with no artifact to metabolize. The skill must stay quiet. The three checks are additive assertions about what the run did INSTEAD of firing: an abstention that also refused to answer, or that bounced the ask back, is not the behaviour this case is asserting. Empty expected_checks would leave the case resting on the runner's non-trigger control flow alone, which validate_prompt_set now rejects.

cases.prompt: summarize the attached changelog in exactly three bullets
cases.rationale: An artifact IS present but the ask is fully specified, which is the near-miss shape most likely to over-trigger. Same additive assertions as negative-01: the run must have stayed quiet AND produced the three bullets rather than asking which changelog.
